scope: Public-source factual register; no private relationship or company-confidential material.

facts.text: Yamaha Motor Co., Ltd. is a distinct company from Yamaha Corporation; this research concerns Yamaha Motor and its identified subsidiaries.
facts.limitation: This package does not assess Yamaha Corporation or infer any relationship between the two companies.

facts.text: Marine is a Yamaha Motor core business and materially contributes to the group: the 2025 Marine plan reports FY2024 consolidated revenue of ¥2,576.2bn and operating income of ¥181.6bn, with Marine shown at 21% of revenue and 48% of operating income.
facts.limitation: The figures are group-plan presentation figures; no standalone Marine capex budget or geographic revenue split is reported.

facts.text: Yamaha Motor’s 2025–2027 Marine plan describes integrated boats, connected products, automated boat control, electric outboards and other efficiency pathways, with external collaboration; it reports R&D expense at 1.7× and capital investment at 1.8× the prior plan.
facts.limitation: A plan is not proof of launch, availability, partner selection, or a commitment to any third party.

facts.text: Yamaha Motor completed its acquisition of Torqeedo in 2024. Official materials describe Torqeedo electric and hybrid drives, batteries, accessories, patents, series-production facilities and R&D, with integrated systems spanning 0.5–100 kW in the acquisition description.
facts.limitation: These capabilities do not establish a third-party-compatible configuration, supply commitment, certification, or warranty arrangement.

facts.text: The current Torqeedo Deep Blue Hybrid page describes 25–100 kW continuous electric motor power at 360 V, 360-V batteries, generator-to-DC-bus integration, CAN/Ethernet, and electric/power/hybrid modes; it lists ferries and water taxis among typical applications.
facts.limitation: Configuration-specific duty cycle, peak values, certification, integration terms and availability must be confirmed; no drop-in fit is established.

facts.text: Yamaha’s marine manufacturing and product footprint includes outboards from 2–450 hp, Japan production at Fukuroi South and Kumamoto, additional outboard production bases in Thailand and Brazil, and boat production at Hokkaido and Amakusa; group boat brands include Skeeter and G3.
facts.limitation: The sources do not establish spare capacity, third-party vessel manufacturing willingness, or suitability for a specific third-party vessel.

facts.text: Helm Master EX publicly lists Yamaha DEC/DES integration, joystick, Course/Heading Hold, Track Point, SetPoint, bow-thruster integration and wireless control for compatible Yamaha outboards. A 2024 presentation separately recorded a GPS-guided autodocking target.
facts.limitation: Current reviewed product pages do not prove general autodocking launch, open APIs, third-party propulsion support, autonomous navigation, or third-party flight-control compatibility.

facts.text: Yamaha’s marine digital activity includes Siren Marine connected monitoring and the Skipperi relationship: Yamaha invested in Skipperi, later established Yamaha Motor Connected Innovation in Finland and acquired fleet-software/IP assets; 2026 materials describe booking, payment, training, access, fuel billing and fleet data functions.
facts.limitation: This demonstrates connected/fleet product activity, not passenger-route concessions, autonomous-vessel capability, charging infrastructure, or third-party integration.

facts.text: Yamaha’s official outboard directory identifies marine distributors in Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam, Taiwan, China, Hong Kong and South Korea; country group-company presence is separately listed and does not by itself prove marine operations.
facts.limitation: A distributor listing is not proof of boatbuilding, operator rights, passenger service, route permits, charging readiness, or spare capacity.

facts.text: Yamaha Motor Ventures is a parent-backed corporate-venture channel: Yamaha’s official 2023 release describes a US$100m, 10-year Exploratory Fund II, while separate materials describe a sustainability fund; official team pages identify current venture leadership.
facts.limitation: Fund size is not a parent operating budget, individual ticket indication, Marine approval, or evidence of willingness to invest in a particular company.
